name: Formoterol
route_note: Dry-powder, metered-dose or nebulised inhalation, typically twice daily; often in combination inhalers
owner: generic (many); combination products by AstraZeneca, Chiesi and others

discovery.note: A formanilide-substituted phenylethanolamine developed in Japan in the 1970s.

tagline: Fast-onset long-acting bronchodilator used in maintenance-and-reliever inhalers
summary: Formoterol is a long-acting beta2-agonist with an onset of action within minutes, comparable to salbutamol, and a duration of about 12 hours. Combined with budesonide it can be used both as maintenance and as an as-needed reliever in asthma, an approach now preferred in GINA guidance.
mechanism: Formoterol is a potent, full agonist at the beta2-adrenergic receptor. Activation increases cAMP and relaxes airway smooth muscle.
Its moderate lipophilicity lets it reach the receptor quickly from the aqueous phase (fast onset) while also forming a membrane depot that sustains activity for around 12 hours.
uses: Maintenance treatment of asthma in combination with an inhaled corticosteroid
Maintenance and reliever therapy (budesonide/formoterol) in asthma

history.title: Symbicort
history.detail: Budesonide/formoterol (Symbicort) is first approved in Europe.

history.title: US approval
history.detail: FDA approves Foradil Aerolizer dry-powder inhaler.

history.title: Symbicort in the US; arformoterol
history.detail: FDA approves Symbicort for asthma and the (R,R)-enantiomer arformoterol (Brovana) for COPD.

history.title: As-needed budesonide/formoterol
history.detail: SYGMA trials published supporting as-needed budesonide/formoterol in mild asthma.

history.title: GINA guidance change
history.detail: GINA stops recommending SABA-only treatment in adults and adolescents, favouring as-needed low-dose ICS/formoterol.

history.title: Triple therapy
history.detail: FDA approves Breztri Aerosphere (budesonide/glycopyrrolate/formoterol) for COPD.

pk.bioavailability: Inhaled: rapidly absorbed; much of the dose swallowed
pk.metabolism: Direct glucuronidation and O-demethylation (CYP2D6, CYP2C19, CYP2C9, CYP2A6)

serious: Asthma-related death if used without an inhaled corticosteroid

facts: Because of its rapid onset, formoterol is the only LABA used in combination inhalers as a reliever.
Arformoterol is the (R,R)-enantiomer of formoterol, marketed separately for nebulisation in COPD.
